title: 27. Toys: Playthings with Know-How
subtitle: What is out there, what suits you, how to use it safely and cleanly, and how to start alone or together. In spicy mode with a step-by-step plan and games for two.

lessons.title: Does It Replace Me?
lessons.summary: Why toys are not a sign of something missing, what they can do and where their limits are.
lessons.content:
Hardly any topic is surrounded by as many prejudices as toys in the bedroom. Some people are ashamed of them, others fear being replaced. Yet a toy is nothing more than a tool: it takes work off your hand, delivers stimulation a hand cannot, and adds variety.

What a toy does well
It delivers steady stimulation without getting tired. A vibration reaches nerve endings that barely respond to pressure alone. It takes pace and performance pressure out of the equation: you don't have to do anything "right", you can simply feel. And it widens your repertoire, alone or together.

What a toy cannot do
It replaces neither closeness nor attention nor a person. It doesn't know what you like today, and it doesn't respond to you. Anyone who only touches themselves with a toy because it is faster sometimes notices that the body gets used to the strong stimulation. Then it helps to practise more often with your hand and without any aids.

Typical worries
"Then I'll always need it." No. Your body learns what you like, and that stays reachable without a toy if you vary things in between.
"Then I'm not good enough." People who know their desire well use toys too, just as someone who loves cooking still owns a blender.
"It's embarrassing." Shame is the most common reason never to try. It is learned, not innate.

The task
Write down what the topic stirs in you: curiosity, worry, shame, desire. One sentence per feeling. Then cross out everything that isn't true when you think honestly. What remains is your starting point for this course.
lessons.reflection_question: Which thought about toys has been loudest so far, and where does it come from?

lessons.title: The Overview: What Is Out There
lessons.summary: The main kinds for women, men and couples and what they are meant for.
lessons.content:
The market is huge and confusing. It helps to sort toys by what they do.

To rest on the body and vibrate
External vibrators and wand vibrators are placed on the outside: on the clitoris and labia, on the glans, shaft, perineum, nipples, or all over the body as a massage. They are the best way in because they leave little room for mistakes. Small ones for travel are called bullets, large wand massagers deliver strong, deep vibration.

Pressure waves and suction
Pressure-wave toys sit over the clitoris and create air pulses without touching the sensitive spot directly. Many find them less "sharp" and yet very intense.

For insertion
Vibrators and dildos for insertion come in different sizes, shapes and firmness. Curved models aim at the front wall of the vagina, where many people have an especially sensitive zone. Love balls are not training devices in a medical sense. For pelvic floor problems, physiotherapy helps more than any gadget, more on that in course 3.

For the penis
Masturbators are soft sleeves with an inner texture. Penis rings keep the blood in the penis longer and can stabilise an erection. Some carry a small vibration that both partners feel when worn during sex.

For the bottom and the prostate
Anal plugs and prostate massagers have a wide base so that nothing can slip inside. More on safety in lesson 4, and on prostate and perineum in course 15.

For couples
Couples' vibrators wrap around both partners or sit between the bodies, vibrating rings are worn by the man, massage candles and oils are sensual starters. Even a blindfold or a feather is a toy.

The task
Pick two kinds that make you curious and just look online at what they look like and what they are for. You don't have to buy anything. This is about orientation.
lessons.reflection_question: Which kind made you most curious, and which put you off?

lessons.title: Material, Care and Lubricant
lessons.summary: Which materials are good for the body, how to clean toys and which lubricant fits.
lessons.content:
Toys touch mucous membranes, so material and care are worth a look. That protects against irritation and infection.

Good materials
Medical-grade or body-safe silicone is soft, smooth and easy to clean. Glass and stainless steel are non-porous, hold warmth and cold and tolerate any lubricant. Hard ABS plastic is cheap and also smooth.

Materials to avoid
Soft, sticky plastics such as jelly or PVC often contain plasticisers, smell strongly of chemicals and are porous. Germs can settle in porous material and cannot be washed out. If you own such a toy, always put a condom over it.

Cleaning
Wash with warm water and mild, fragrance-free soap before and after every use and dry well. Special toy cleaners work too. Silicone, glass and stainless steel can also be briefly rinsed in hot water if the manufacturer allows it. Never put electronic toys in boiling water and never submerge the charging port. Check the waterproof rating.

From bottom to vagina
A toy that has been in the bottom never goes into the vagina or the mouth unwashed. Safer is a fresh condom or a separate toy for each purpose.

Lubricant
Water-based lubricant suits all materials and is the safe standard. Silicone lubricant lasts longer but attacks silicone toys, making them sticky and rough. It is fine with glass, steel and ABS. Oil-based products, including massage oil or coconut oil, are unsuitable for condoms and often stay on mucous membranes longer. For sensitive skin, avoid fragrance and warming or cooling effects.

Storing
Dry, separate from each other and not touching, because silicone toys can discolour or deform on contact. One cloth bag per toy is ideal.

The task
Look at the toys you own or imagine owning: what are they made of? If you find no information, treat them like porous toys and use a condom.
lessons.reflection_question: What about care and material was new to you, and what will you change as a result?

lessons.title: Safety: Where It Gets Tricky
lessons.summary: Anal toys, penis rings and other things where mistakes can hurt, with clear rules.
lessons.content:
Most toys are harmless. In a few places, though, accidents happen again and again that could easily be avoided.

Anal toys
In the bottom, one iron rule applies: only toys with a wide base or handle that stays outside. The rectum has no floor, and an object without a base can slide in so far that it can't be grasped any more. Then only the emergency room helps, and it is there for exactly this, without blame.
Start small and with plenty of lubricant. The sphincter needs time. Breathe out deeply as you insert and stop at pain. Numbing gels are off limits, because pain is the warning you need.

No household objects
Bottles, vegetables, pens, hairbrushes and the like are not toys. They are too hard, too rough, cannot be cleaned or break. The most common problem in emergency rooms is exactly such things.

Penis rings
A penis ring should be stretchy and soft, ideally silicone, not rigid metal. It comes off after twenty to thirty minutes at most, and immediately if there is coldness, numbness, pain or discolouration. Small sizes are dangerous: if the ring won't come off, that is an emergency. Anyone taking blood thinners or with circulation problems asks their doctor first.
If an erection lasts longer than four hours or hurts, go to the emergency room.

Vacuum pumps and strong suction toys
They may only be used briefly and with little vacuum. Redness is normal, bruises or pain are not.

Vibration and habituation
Permanent top speed can dull sensitivity for a while. Give yourself breaks and vary the intensity.

Devices and power
Don't charge batteries in the heat and dispose of damaged devices. Never use battery toys with leaked batteries. Electro-stimulation toys don't belong near the heart or head, and certainly not in beginners' hands.

The task
Make yourself a safety list: lubricant ready, toy clean, base on anal toys, a time limit for rings, a phone within reach. That takes the worry away in the moment itself.
lessons.reflection_question: Which of these rules didn't you know, and how will you make sure it holds in the heat of the moment?

lessons.title: Buying, Storing, Staying Discreet
lessons.summary: What to look for when buying, how to store toys inconspicuously and how to stay safe with app toys.
lessons.content:
With toys, quality pays. Cheap goods from dubious sources are often made of poor material and offer no safety.

Where to buy
Reputable specialist shops and online stores with an imprint, return policy and clear material information. Many ship in plain packaging with an inconspicuous sender. Look for hints such as "body-safe", "phthalate-free" and "latex-free". If a price seems too good to be true, be careful.

What to check
Size and weight, noise level (quiet motors are a blessing in thin-walled flats), rechargeable or battery, waterproofing, a travel lock against accidental switching on, and whether parts can be exchanged or replaced.

Start small
Your first toy doesn't have to be the most expensive or the biggest. A small, well-made external vibrator is often enough to find out whether you like vibration at all.

Storing it discreetly
A cloth bag in a drawer or box, not lying open in the bedside table, especially when children or guests are around. Anything that needs power is stored so it can't switch on by accident. Put lubricant and cleaner with it, so everything is in one place.

App toys and remote control
Toys with Bluetooth or an app can be controlled from afar. That is tempting but raises privacy questions: read what data the app collects, don't use accounts with your real name, and only give access to people you trust. Connections over the internet can be intercepted if they are not encrypted. When in doubt, Bluetooth range within the same room is the safer choice.

When you no longer need it
Toys are not given away or resold, but cleaned and thrown out with household waste, or, if they contain a battery, taken to an electronics collection point.

The task
Write down what your first toy should do, a budget and two things it must never be. Then search with a clear aim.
lessons.reflection_question: What should your first toy do for you, and what would be a dealbreaker?

lessons.title: Talking About It Together
lessons.summary: How to bring up toys without anyone feeling devalued, and how to start together.
lessons.content:
The conversation is often harder than the toy itself. Whoever voices the wish fears hurting the other. Whoever hears it asks: "Am I not enough?"

The right opening
Start with what you wish for, not with what you lack. Instead of "I come so rarely" say: "I'm curious about something new with you." Instead of "It doesn't work with my hand" say: "I'd like to try something that gives us both more room."

Addressing the worry
If your partner hesitates, ask: "What worries you?" Often behind it is the thought of being replaced. Say clearly that this is about adding, not replacing. And listen without persuading. A no is a no, perhaps only for today.

For the leader and the hesitant
The hesitant one decides how far it goes. One option: the toy comes into the room but stays in the bedside table for now. Or it is tried only on a body part that seems unproblematic to both, such as the back, the feet or the shoulders. That turns a question into a game.

Choosing together
Look at pictures together and each say what appeals and what doesn't. Use the app's yes/no list to tick independently what interests you. You only see where you overlap. That takes off pressure.

Rules for the first time
Everyone may stop at any time. Whoever holds the toy follows the other, not their own pace. One word, for example "pause", is enough. Afterwards you talk about what you experienced, without judging.

The task
Have the conversation this week. Use the sentences above as an opening. You don't have to get a toy or decide anything. The aim is that both can openly say what they think.
lessons.reflection_question: What worry did your partner voice, and what did it show you about your trust?

lessons.title: Alone with a Toy: A Step-by-Step Plan
lessons.summary: In five steps from the first play with an external vibrator to combining it with edging and fantasy.
lessons.content:
The introduction in Spicy Solo (the lesson "Toys: an Introduction Without Shame") showed you which toys exist. Here is a plan that takes you over five evenings from careful to bold.

Step one: curiosity
The toy runs on the lowest setting and first lies next to the most sensitive spot. You only move along the outside: thighs, belly, groin and nipples. It isn't about an orgasm yet, only about feeling.

Step two: approach
You place the toy on the most sensitive spot, the clitoris, glans or frenulum, and let it rest there. Move not the toy but yourself. Try three intensities and note how each one feels.

Step three: waves
Combine the toy with the edging from Spicy Solo. Bring yourself to an eight on the scale, take the toy away, let the heat sink, start again. After three waves you decide whether to come.

Step four: fantasy
Switch your imagination on. You can play through a scene or imagine someone else's hands. The toy may play the role you like.

Step five: without a toy
To finish, you touch yourself with your hand and ask what you can take from the toy: pace, pressure, spot. That way you stay independent.

Very spicy: words for the steps
Imagine someone speaking to you. For example: "I want to watch you put the vibrator on your clit and not be able to stay calm." "Turn it on slowly, I want to hear you start to moan." "I want you to tremble before you're allowed to come." If you prefer to keep it to yourself, whisper such sentences to yourself.

If it goes too fast
Many come within minutes with toys. That is fine. If you want to enjoy longer, change the pace, take the toy away briefly or press gently with your palm against the pelvic floor until the wave subsides.

Hygiene at the end
Wash the toy and your hands before you fall asleep or return to everyday life. Never apply a lubricant that doesn't suit the material, see lesson 3.

lessons.title: Together with a Toy: Leading and Being Led
lessons.summary: Games with toys in bed: watching, remote control, combining with mouth and hand.
lessons.content:
Toys in a shared bed are not a stopgap but a playground of their own. The basics are in Spicy for Two ("Toys in the Shared Bed"). Here are four games that build on it.

Game one: the other's hand
One person lies back, the other guides the toy. The one lying says "warmer" or "colder", nothing more. After ten minutes you swap. That way you learn how the other side hears, without anyone having to explain at length.

Game two: watching
One person uses the toy on themselves, the other only watches and keeps their hands still for ten minutes. Many find being seen hot, and for the watcher restraint is the spice. Afterwards they may join in.

Game three: remote control
If the toy has a remote, one person wears it in daily life or at home, the other holds the control. Agree beforehand where and when, and that one word ends everything at any time. In public, only use volume and intensity that nobody notices.

Game four: together
Couples' vibrators and vibrating rings are worn during sex. Try your favourite position where both have access. Who comes first doesn't matter.

Very spicy: how it sounds
Whoever leads may talk: "Hold still, I want to see you squirm." "Tell me how wet you are." "You can only come when I say so." "Show me how you fuck yourself, I'm watching." Whoever is led answers with "More", "Slower" or "Please". Clarify beforehand which words you like.

Before you start
Talk about limits and a stop word beforehand. Use plenty of lubricant and mind the material. And never move a toy from the bottom to the vagina without cleaning it or putting on a new condom.

Aftercare
After intense play, closeness feels good: a blanket, water, a few minutes in each other's arms. Talk briefly about what you liked. That makes the next round easier.
